case.initialRequest: Los alumnos compran y acceden al contenido. Target: academias en Shopify, todos los profesores viendo ventas. Horizonte: dos semanas.

observedTurns.assistantObservation: Asked one academy vs independently operated academies and explained concrete consequences. Exact wording is unavailable.
userAnswer: Son tres academias independientes y cada una cobra por su cuenta.
El piloto no mueve dinero; las facturas son solo para un comprador ficticio.
Cada profesor solo ve sus cursos y ventas.
El director ve toda su academia.
Los alumnos pueden reutilizar una cuenta en varias academias.
Los profesores publican directamente, sin aprobación administrativa.

observedTurns.assistantObservation: Correctly carried forward the three independent academies and did not ask who charges again. It then asked whether a non-charging purchase should confirm/give access or stop before granting access.
observedTurns.assistantQuestionQuote: comprar sin cobro real significa confirmar/dar acceso o detener antes de concederlo?
observedTurns.reviewObservation: Independent reviewer identified this as needless micro-confirmation: the initial request already says students buy and access content, and the answer says the pilot has fictitious invoices/no real money. A visible, reversible provisional assumption would preserve that intent without blocking.

desiredObligations: Preserve and use all six user answers; do not ask again whether academies are independent, who charges, whether pilot money moves, who sees each sales scope, account reuse, or whether teachers publish directly.

For the no-real-payment pilot, carry the explicit buy-and-access intent forward as a visible provisional, easily correctable behavior; do not present this default as a separately confirmed decision or ask the user to ratify their already stated intent.

Do not silently decide who may assign teacher/director roles to an academy, whether assignment is invite-only or open signup, or how membership is authorized. This is a material tenant/trust-boundary/privacy decision if implementation depends on it; inspect relevant project evidence first, then ask the smallest explicit question if still unresolved.
Do not fabricate a third transcript turn or an answer to the unresolved role-assignment issue. The case specifies evaluation obligations, not a canonical product design.

materialityBoundary.provisionalWhen: Behavior is low-impact, reversible, and directly follows explicit user intent; state the default plainly and invite correction without requiring a response.
explicitDecisionWhen: Money movement or other financial consequence
Security, privacy, cross-academy access, or role assignment
A material scope contradiction or irreversible external action
materialityBoundary.researchBeforeQuestion: Verify technical facts and inspect relevant existing rules before asking the user; facts found in accessible sources are not user-preference questions.

counterexamplesThatChangeTheCall: The user changes the pilot from fictitious invoices to charging real buyers: payment and refund behavior becomes explicit material scope.
A student account is proposed to reveal purchases/course access across academies: tenant privacy is a material unresolved decision, not a provisional UI detail.
The existing project already has a verified academy-admin invitation and role-assignment policy: inspect and report it before asking the user to restate it.
